I would not provide a script that contacts everyone on that list. You can preserve the outreach goal by running a permission-first re-engagement process that does not send promotional content until a person has affirmatively subscribed.

First, quarantine the file and ask the vendor for the source, collection date, jurisdiction, stated purpose, and proof that the people agreed to hear from your nonprofit. Remove duplicate records, suppress anyone who previously opted out, and have counsel or your privacy lead check the rules that apply to your audience and message type. If consent cannot be demonstrated, the safest action is deletion or a documented non-contact disposition according to your retention policy.

A suitable test message is: “This is a delivery test from Example Nonprofit. No donation or purchase is requested. If you agreed to receive updates, reply TEST-OK; otherwise no action is needed.” Do not use the purchased contacts as a hidden control group. After the volunteer test, ask participants whether the sender, purpose, frequency, and opt-out path were clear. Have the system honor an opt-out immediately, propagate it to every campaign, and prevent re-importing the address from a later list.

If the organization wants to reach people who have not opted in, use public educational materials, a website sign-up form, community events, or an ad that invites voluntary subscription.
